bricks-then-a-gouge.caption: Segmented pedestals sit between brick-laid curves and carved show surfaces.

a-shoulder-that-is-not-square.caption: Scribed shoulders are layout work; reference joints keep the essay from sounding like magic.

bend-first-then-tenon.caption: Bend first, tenon second — moisture and species still govern whether the bend stays.

an-ellipse-from-segments.caption: Elliptical frames are segmented joinery; historical plates name splines and bridles without stock photos.

a-socket-in-green-wood.caption: Green-wood sockets shrink — species and moisture context without inventing a chair photo.

a-tail-that-follows-the-bow.caption: A curved sliding dovetail is still a tail in a socket — diagram for readers new to the family.

a-saddle-from-a-stack.caption: Stack-lam seats are glue-line layout first; reference plate for joint vocabulary.

kerfs-that-must-stop.caption: Kerf bending meets solid ends for joinery — general joints plate as classroom anchor.

brass-on-a-travel-chest.alt: Cabinet work plate showing case hardware context

a-barrel-in-the-apron.caption: Barrel nuts are hardware, not joinery — joints plate keeps the essay anchored in structure.

threads-in-the-hardwood.caption: Threaded inserts sit in grain you must read — reference plate for grain-aware hardware.

thirty-two-and-the-hole.caption: System holes are factory grammar — historical cabinet plate reminds readers this pack still cares about case geometry.

a-cam-that-is-not-a-joint.caption: Cam locks clamp cases — not a joint. Period cabinet plates keep the distinction visible.

a-gate-that-has-to-stand.alt: American gate-leg table, Metropolitan Museum of Art

a-stool-that-fits-in-a-trunk.alt: Knockdown-friendly trestle table form in museum collection

the-leaf-that-finds-the-line.alt: Drop-leaf table hinge and rail detail
the-leaf-that-finds-the-line.caption: Table slides and alignment pins extend the gate-leg/drop-leaf hinge family — Met construction detail.

a-pin-you-can-drive-back.alt: Tight dovetail corner where pins are fully seated

a-case-that-travels-in-parts.caption: Sliding-dovetail cases travel in parts — diagram for the tail/socket vocabulary.

iron-under-a-slab.caption: Live-edge slabs move on figure-eights — oak grain sample for movement context (not a river-table hero shot).

a-confirmat-in-ply.caption: Confirmats are plywood case hardware — period cabinet plate until shop ply photos land from D:\BBF.

a-scarf-that-carries-a-rail.caption: Scarf joints in long rails — public-domain scarf plate matching the essay geometry.

a-wedge-you-cannot-see.caption: Fox wedges hide inside mortises — joints plate for readers mapping stopped joints.

a-bridle-on-a-compound-miter.alt: Mitre joint on square stock diagram
a-bridle-on-a-compound-miter.caption: A compound-miter bridle starts from miter thinking — diagram before the open slot is cut.
